newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain truckers give mild welcome to fuel measures.
newsitem.headline: Spain truckers give mild welcome to fuel measures.

text.p: Striking truckers gave a cautious welcome on Friday to a Spanish cabinet decree introducing deregulatory measures aimed at lowering the costs of fuel distribution.
Striking truckers, who have demanded measures to curb surging fuel costs, said the move only partly met their requests.

"The measure is one we requested, but we're also asking for other things and, aside from that we'd like to have professional fuel prices, with a subsidy, such as other sectors like farming and fisheries," said Jose Manuel Martinez spokesman for Fedetrans transport union.
But at present around 80 percent of truckers operate independently and, along with small customers, they have to buy fuel at petrol stations at current prices.
"These will have to join a cooperative," Martinez said.
Earlier, Industry Minister Josep Pique said "these measures aim to increase competition in the distribution process and are expected, logically, to have a positive impact on prices."
Pique said the measures would impact on the transportation of goods and passengers, as well as marine transportation, and should save cooperatives five to 10 pesetas per litre on diesel.
